title: Corporate Travel, Meal and Business Expense Reimbursement Policy

sections.content: This policy governs the reimbursement of travel, lodging, meals, and business entertainment incurred during company business. All expense claims must be submitted via the Concur Expense portal within 30 calendar days of expense incurrence. Claims submitted beyond 60 days require VP Finance authorization.

Employees traveling on domestic flights or international flights under 6 hours duration must book Economy Class. Business Class bookings are permitted only for nonstop flight legs exceeding 6 continuous flight hours, or when medically necessary with Occupational Health documentation and CFO sign-off.

Maximum allowable nightly hotel rates (excluding local taxes) are categorized by geographic tier: Tier 1 High-Cost Metro Areas (New York, London, San Francisco, Tokyo, Singapore): $280 USD per night. Tier 2 Standard Metro Areas: $190 USD per night. Tier 3 Regional Cities: $140 USD per night. Bookings exceeding caps by more than 15% require Department VP pre-approval.

Employees are provided daily per-diem meal allowances as follows: Tier 1 Cities: $85 USD per full travel day ($20 Breakfast, $25 Lunch, $40 Dinner). Tier 2 and Tier 3 Cities: $65 USD per full travel day ($15 Breakfast, $20 Lunch, $30 Dinner). Itemized receipts are mandatory for any individual business meal or transaction exceeding $25 USD. Alcohol is not reimbursable without client presence.

Use of rideshare (Uber/Lyft Standard) and public rapid transit is encouraged. Luxury or Black car services are non-reimbursable. Personal vehicle mileage for business travel is reimbursed at the statutory rate of $0.67 USD per mile, excluding regular daily home-to-office commutes.

title: Corporate Procurement, Vendor Selection and Supplier Payment Guidelines

sections.section_title: 1. Purchase Order (PO) Thresholds and Approval Ladder
sections.content: All vendor purchases exceeding $2,500 USD require an approved Purchase Order before contract signing or service commencement. Approval limits are structured as follows: Tier A (Up to $10,000 USD): Department Manager approval; Tier B ($10,001 to $50,000 USD): Department Director approval; Tier C ($50,001 to $250,000 USD): VP and Head of Procurement approval; Tier D (Exceeding $250,000 USD): Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) formal sign-off.

For any procurement contract with an aggregate contract value exceeding $50,000 USD, the procurement team must solicit a minimum of three independent, sealed competitive bids (RFP/RFQ). Single-source or sole-source exemptions require a formally documented Sole Source Justification memo approved by the General Counsel.

Accounts Payable enforces strict Three-Way Matching before any vendor invoice is disbursed. The accounts payable system automatically cross-references: 1. The approved Purchase Order; 2. The Goods Received Note (GRN) or signed milestone proof-of-performance; 3. The vendor's itemized commercial tax invoice. Payment is halted automatically if price variance exceeds 1.5% or quantity exceeds 0%.

sections.section_title: 4. Standard Payment Terms and Wire Transfer Anti-Fraud
sections.content: Corporate standard payment terms are Net 45 days from the receipt of a verified invoice. Net 30 or Net 15 terms require Treasury Director sign-off. Wire transfer bank routing changes requested by any vendor require telephone callback verification to the verified vendor finance officer on record before updating banking records.

title: Capital Expenditure (CapEx) Governance and Asset Depreciation Manual

sections.section_title: 1. Capital Expenditure Definition and Capitalization Floor
sections.content: Tangible assets or software development expenditures with an acquisition cost of $5,000 USD or greater and an estimated useful operational lifespan exceeding 12 months must be capitalized as fixed assets rather than expensed as operating expenditure (OpEx). Items under $5,000 are expensed immediately.

CapEx projects between $50,000 and $200,000 require Capital Budgeting Committee approval and a Return on Investment (ROI) payback period under 36 months. Projects exceeding $500,000 require Board of Directors Audit Committee ratification.
key_entities: Board of Directors Audit Committee over $500,000

sections.content: Depreciation is recognized using the straight-line method over statutory useful lives: Computer Hardware & Servers: 3 years (36 months); Enterprise Software Licenses: 5 years (60 months); Office Furniture and Fixtures: 7 years; Leasehold Improvements: Lesser of 10 years or remaining lease term.
